newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks fall again as govt offers no relief.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks fall again as govt offers no relief.

text.p: Japanese stocks took another steep tumble on Monday as the government failed to offer new economic initiatives in a closely watched policy speech and reaffirmed its resolve to raise taxes.

The key Nikkei stock index closed just over 600 points down, but off its lows, reflecting disappointment with a speech to parliament in which Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto vowed to press ahead with tax increases and repeated pledges of broad reforms.

The market's key barometer, the Nikkei 225 average, closed down 609.70 points, or 3.37 percent, at 17,480.34. It had briefly plunged to 17,237.27 -- a drop of around 850 points -- ahead of the speech, as the market guessed accurately that Hashimoto would have little new to say to bolster confidence in the stock market.

The slide was also fuelled by news that major sushi chain operator Kyotaru Co Ltd had filed for court protection from creditors with debts of some $865 million in yet another big Japanese business failure.
"It's unlikely that anything that could have a quick impact on the market will come up soon," said Takashi Kanasaki, managing director of Yamaichi Securities.

The Nikkei plunged more than 2,000 points in the first trading week of this year on worries that the government's forthcoming tax increases could derail Japan's fragile economic recovery, but it recovered some ground last week.
